key_insight: Instead of relying on repeated random sampling, the paper shows that LLM reasoning can be improved by learning a small search policy that generates diverse semantic concepts, hints, or strategies to guide answer generation.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical way to spend test-time compute more effectively: optimize a lightweight concept generator once, then reuse it to boost hard reasoning performance across larger frozen LLMs.
method: Sample diverse concepts/strategies first, then condition answer generation on them.
Use a multi-concept trajectory to increase exploration beyond near-duplicate decodes.
Train the concept generator with reinforcement learning so its outputs maximize downstream success of a fixed answer model.
evidence_signal: On hard mathematical reasoning tasks, the trained concept generator improved pass@k over naive repeated sampling at the same answer-generation budget, outperformed concepts from much larger untuned models, and transferred to unseen answer models including a different family.
watch_item: The approach depends on a separately trained concept generator and careful reward design, so gains may be sensitive to training setup and may not transfer equally well outside the evaluated reasoning domain.
paper_title: Beyond Repeated Sampling: Learning Search Policies for LLM Reasoning
